transcript.content: "Hi, I'm planning a flight to Athens with Sky Airways and I was wondering if I can get some information on wheelchair assistance for my journey? I use a wheelchair due to mobility issues and would need help getting through check-in and onto the plane."
Thank you for calling Sky Airways customer service. My name is Sky, and I'm here to help you today. How can I assist you?

"I'd appreciate it if you could tell me what types of wheelchair assistance are available on your flights, such as pre-boarding or assistance at check-in, and whether there's a fee associated with it."
Certainly, I can help you with that. I will look up the information regarding wheelchair assistance for your journey.
"That would be great, Sky. Can you also please let me know how far in advance I need to request this assistance and if there's a specific form or process I need to fill out?"

Sky Airways offers several types of wheelchair assistance, including help for those who can walk short distances, those who cannot climb steps, and those who are immobile and require assistance throughout their journey. This assistance is generally free of charge.

You need to request special assistance at least 48 hours before your flight, or 72 hours for more complex needs. You can do this by contacting our accessibility team or by adding the assistance when you book your flight.

"That sounds great, thank you Sky. Just to confirm, if I have a more complex need, such as being immobile and requiring assistance throughout my journey, is there a specific form or process that I would need to go through when booking my flight, or can I request this assistance directly with the accessibility team?"

For complex needs, such as requiring assistance throughout your journey due to immobility, you should request this at least 72 hours before departure. You can either contact our accessibility team directly or add the assistance when you are booking your flight. There isn't a specific form beyond that process.

"Okay, thank you for clarifying that. Just to confirm, my name is Emily Wilson, and I'll be flying from London to Athens in about two weeks. Can you please just repeat back to me what I've discussed so far, including the types of wheelchair assistance available, the process for requesting it, and the deadlines?"

Certainly, Emily. To recap, Sky Airways offers different levels of wheelchair assistance. WCHR is for passengers who can walk short distances but need a wheelchair for longer ones in the terminal. WCHS is for those who cannot climb steps or walk long distances, providing assistance from check-in to your seat. WCHC is for passengers who are immobile and require assistance throughout, and for this, you would need to travel with a carer.

You should request special assistance at least 48 hours before departure, or 72 hours for more complex needs like WCHC. You can do this by contacting our accessibility team directly or by adding the assistance when you book your flight. This service is generally free of charge, with the exception of unaccompanied minors.

"Thank you for explaining all that, Sky. I think WCHC would be my best option since I'm immobile and would need assistance throughout the journey. Can you please confirm that I won't have to book a companion with me, or is there anything else I should know about traveling with a carer?"

For the WCHC assistance type, which is for passengers who are immobile and require assistance throughout their journey, you must travel with a carer. This is a requirement to ensure your safety and comfort during the flight.

"I understand that having a carer with me is required for WCHC assistance. I don't have one available at the moment, but I'd like to ask if there are any options for booking a companion or arranging alternative care before my trip?"

Sky Airways does not provide or arrange for carers or companions. If you require WCHC assistance, you must travel with your own carer. I recommend you make arrangements for a carer before your flight, as this is a requirement for WCHC assistance.

"I understand that Sky Airways doesn't provide or arrange carers, and I appreciate your recommendation to make arrangements beforehand. However, I was hoping to get some more general information on what I can expect in terms of support and services during my flight. Can you tell me a bit about how the WCHC assistance would be handled from check-in to boarding?"

With WCHC assistance, you will receive support throughout your journey, from check-in right through to your seat on the aircraft. This includes assistance with navigating the airport, going through security, and boarding the plane. As previously mentioned, for WCHC assistance, you must travel with a carer as you are immobile and require assistance throughout.

"Thank you for explaining that again, Sky. I think I understand now. Just to confirm, when I request WCHC assistance at least 72 hours before my flight, will I also need to provide information about my carer, such as their contact details or medical clearance, if necessary?"

The information I have about our special assistance policy does not specify whether you need to provide details about your carer, such as their contact information or medical clearance, when requesting WCHC assistance. I recommend contacting our accessibility team directly for these specific details to ensure all arrangements are made correctly for your journey.

"Okay, that makes sense. Well, I think I've got a good understanding of what's involved with WCHC assistance now. Thank you so much for your help, Sky. I'll definitely reach out to the accessibility team directly to confirm all the details and make sure everything is arranged correctly."
